tools.name: search_events
tools.description:
Search Spanish commercial-registry (BORME) events, newest first, as JSON.

All filters are optional (see each parameter); coverage starts in 2009.
Returns at most `limit` events.

Barcelona prints some acts as free text under "Otros conceptos": recognised
wording gets its own act type (act_type_raw stays "Otros conceptos";
fields.shareholder names a sole shareholder when the text does), and a
same-entry revocation and reappointment becomes RE_ELECTIONS. Reprocessed
events keep their event_id, but their acts can change.

Without an API key this is the free plan: only the last 7 days, stated in
plan_window. Send your key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account) for your plan's window (full history on pro).

An empty page may carry hidden_by_plan: matches before the plan's window
(matches_before_window, matches_is_at_least, newest_hidden_date) and a note
to pass on. Do not infer from an empty page that no matching events exist.

date_from.title: Date From
date_from.description: Earliest publication date, YYYY-MM-DD (data starts in 2009).

provinces.title: Provinces
provinces.description: BORME province names, accent- and case-insensitive, e.g. MADRID, CADIZ, VIZCAYA. An autonomous community stands for all of its provinces, e.g. Basque Country, Cataluña, Andalucía.

act_types.title: Act Types
act_types.description: Act types, e.g. INCORPORATION, APPOINTMENTS, TERMINATIONS, CAPITAL_INCREASE, DISSOLUTION, INSOLVENCY_STATUS (full list: list_act_types).

company_name_contains.title: Company Name Contains
company_name_contains.description: Part of the company name, at least 3 letters or digits, case-insensitive; % and _ match literally.

tools.name: company_history
tools.description:
Registry timeline for one company, as JSON.

`company` is a slug or a name; a name with several matches returns the
candidate slugs instead. An older slug of a merged company returns the
merged company's whole timeline: company_slug is the current slug,
former_slugs the others, and each event keeps the slug it was printed under.

total_events, first_seen and last_seen describe the whole timeline within
your plan's window, not just this page; truncated is true when the page
holds fewer events than total_events, and next_offset starts the next page
(null on the last). Page with order and offset.

Without an API key this is the free plan: only the last 7 days. Send your
key in the X-API-Key header (https://bormeapi.com/account) for your plan's
window (full history back to 2009 on pro).

company.title: Company
company.description: Company slug (e.g. vaz-metales-sl) or name; a name falls back to a case-insensitive search (at least 3 letters or digits).

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Events to skip, 0-10000, in steps of limit.

tools.name: company_by_nif
tools.description:
Look up a Spanish company by its NIF/CIF tax ID.

Needs the basic plan or higher: send your API key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account).

BORME itself has no dedicated tax-ID field: the mapping is cross-referenced
from open official sources and, in some cases, taken from the text of BORME
notices (more than 580,000 NIF mappings from public sources, still a
minority of companies). A miss means "not matched yet", not "does not
exist". On a hit, use company_history with the returned slug.

If nif_caveat is present, say so and do not present the mapping as settled.
A miss with reason "nif_check_character_failed" is an identifier never
issued to anyone: relay that, the corrected identifier and did_you_mean.
A miss with reason "not_registry_entity" has entity_type (the kind of
entity or person): explain it as the response's note does.
If ambiguous is true, list the candidates and ask which company is meant
(records on one registry sheet in one province are one company).

nif.title: Nif
nif.description: NIF/CIF, e.g. B12345674. Spaces, hyphens, dots and the ES VAT prefix (ESB12345674) are accepted; other country prefixes are not.

tools.name: brand_owner
tools.description:
Find the Spanish company a brand or trading name is linked to, by holder name.

Searches the patent office's trademarks and commercial names (1987 to
today), which BORME does not print, and returns for each the company whose
name matches the holder name the office published.

`commercial_name` identifies a business; `trademark` distinguishes goods or
services (NESCAFÉ is not another name for Nestlé). Say which kind a hit is;
do not say a company "is called" X when X is one of its products.

Links are made on a normalised company name only (the office publishes no
tax IDs) and only where exactly one company or registry sheet fits: present
a hit as a name match, not confirmed ownership. On a hit, use
company_history with the slug.

Needs the basic plan or higher: send your API key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account).

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Brand or trading name, or part of it.

tools.name: company_brands
tools.description:
Trademarks and trading names linked to one company by name (slug from company_history).

Answers "which trading names and trademarks does the patent office list
under a holder of this company's name". The office publishes no tax IDs,
so every link is a name match, not confirmed ownership. Commercial names
identify a business; trademarks distinguish goods or services. An empty
result is ordinary — most companies have neither on file.

`limit` applies to each kind separately (newest first), so trademarks
never push trading names out. `counts` is how many of each kind this
answer lists, not the company's total: when `truncated` is true for a
kind, more are linked than were returned — raise `limit` to see them.

Needs the basic plan or higher: send your API key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account).

company.title: Company
company.description: Company slug, as returned by search_companies or company_history.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum results per kind (trademarks, trading names), 1-200 (default 50).

tools.name: recent_signals
tools.description:
Sample of the latest derived risk signals (last 7 publication days,
max 10 rows). Types: INSOLVENCY_FILED, ACCORDION, MASS_EXIT,
OWNERSHIP_CHANGE, DISTRESS_COMBO, PHOENIX, ADDRESS_CLUSTER, AEAT_DEBTOR,
PUBLIC_CONTRACT_AWARD.

AEAT_DEBTOR comes from the AEAT's yearly debtors list (art. 95 bis LGT):
details carry listed_on, list_year and is_current_list (true for 12 months
from listed_on, a window this API sets). debt_eur is the published total of
tax debts and penalties at 31 December of the year before publication. Say
the company was on the list published on that date; never say the debt is
still outstanding. Only companies in the Registro Mercantil matched by NIF
are covered.

Needs the risk plan: send your API key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account). The full history is in the hosted API's
/v1/signals.

signal_type.title: Signal Type
signal_type.description: One signal type to filter by (see the tool description); omit for all types.

tools.name: daily_digest
tools.description:
Digest of one BORME publication day: totals by event type, top
provinces, and `insolvencies`: every event of the day whose act types
include INSOLVENCY_DECLARATION or INSOLVENCY_STATUS, with company and
province only (SUSPENSION_OF_PAYMENTS, BANKRUPTCY_LEGACY and
PROVISIONAL_SHEET_CLOSURE_INSOLVENCY are not listed).

An INSOLVENCY_STATUS (Situación concursal) notice can record any stage of
the proceedings, from a request for a declaration to the conclusion. Call
the entries insolvency-proceedings notices; before saying a company was
declared insolvent, read its act's payload with search_events (date_from =
date_to = that day, both act types, company_name_contains).

Without an API key this is the free plan: only publication days within the
last 7 days. Send your key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account) for your plan's window.

date.title: Date
date.description: Publication day, YYYY-MM-DD; omit for the latest day in the database.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description:
Find Spanish companies by name and return ranked company cards (slug,
status, province). Use it first when the user gives a company name, then
company_history with the slug.

Matches current names, former names and name variants, ignoring accents,
case, punctuation and the legal form. Each card's `match` is exact, prefix,
contains or fuzzy (only when nothing else matched: a lead, not an
identification; say so); `matched_on` says which name matched. Ranked by
match, then active companies first, then the newest act.

Plans: the free plan's events cover 7 days, but this search is not limited
by history. Without a key a search shows 5 cards and `hidden_by_plan` counts
the rest (`matches_beyond_limit`, a lower bound when `matches_is_at_least`):
relay its note. The NIF is on the card from the basic plan up: send your
key in the X-API-Key header. An empty answer is not proof that a business
does not exist; relay the response's `note` in the user's language.

name.title: Name
name.description: Company name or part of it, at least 3 letters or digits; accents, case, punctuation and legal form are ignored.

province.title: Province
province.description: The company's province, accent-insensitive, e.g. MADRID, VIZCAYA, or an autonomous community for all of its provinces, e.g. Catalonia; several values can be separated by commas, e.g. BIZKAIA,GIPUZKOA. Applied to the candidates the search reads (2,000 with a filter), so a broad name can return fewer companies than match it.

status.title: Status
status.description: One of active, dissolved, extinct, sheet_closed; applied like province.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Cards to skip. At most 200 cards are ranked; truncated true means more candidates existed, so add another word from the name.

tools.name: list_act_types
tools.description:
All normalized event types: the enum (act_type), the original Spanish
label (spanish) and its English label (english).

tools.name: registry_stats
tools.description:
Coverage and freshness report for the BORME dataset behind this server.

Returns a JSON object with: events_approx and companies_approx (planner
estimates, not exact tallies), coverage {from, to} (first and latest
publication day held, YYYY-MM-DD), parse_completeness_last_30d (share of
gazette text successfully structured over the last 30 publication days,
e.g. 0.9987) and source. Open to everyone; no key needed.

Use this to answer "how much data is there?", "how fresh is it?" and
"can I trust date filters for period X?" before running searches. Takes
no arguments; counts are estimates (fast reads), not exact tallies.
